examples.trans: Yes, and she also negotiated a good bonus for you.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и выпросить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and begged on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Перемены могут начаться абсолютно в любой момент.
examples.trans: Changes can begin at absolutely any moment.

examples.text: Мы стали частью большой ресторанной сети.
examples.trans: We have become part of a large restaurant chain.

examples.text: Вот твой новый электронный пропуск, держи.
examples.trans: Here is your new electronic pass, take it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы что, теперь на заводе работаем?
examples.trans: What, do we work at a factory now?

examples.text: Теперь у нашего ресторана совсем другие хозяева.
examples.trans: Now our restaurant has completely different owners.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.text: Привет, девочки! Я так рада вас видеть!
examples.trans: Hi, girls! I am so glad to see you!

examples.text: Я вас тоже так рада всех видеть!
examples.trans: I am so glad to see all of you too!

examples.text: Я вижу машинку.
examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Когда ты нервничаешь, у тебя ус дёргается.

examples.text: Что, думаешь, я слепая и ничего не вижу?
examples.trans: What, do you think I am blind and see nothing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will work out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.text: Если хочешь получить бонус, соблюдай установленные правила.
examples.trans: If you want to get the bonus, follow the established rules.

examples.text: Всё получится!
examples.trans: It will all work out!

examples.text: Из него получится хороший врач.
examples.trans: He'll make a good doctor.

meanings.en: sometimes, from time to time, occasionally
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'sometimes, at times', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Иногда всё может поменяться за одну секунду.
examples.trans: Sometimes everything can change in a single second.

examples.text: Иногда мы делаем глупости.
examples.trans: Sometimes we do foolish things.

examples.text: Иногда наши победы бывают слишком странными.
examples.trans: Sometimes our victories turn out too strange.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vika, may I have a word with you for one second?

examples.text: Человек с чемоданом легко может передумать и остаться.
examples.trans: A man with a suitcase can easily change his mind and stay.

examples.text: Человек с чемоданом легко может передумать и остаться.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the main thing').

examples.trans: But the main thing is that you betrayed your principles.

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'время').

examples.trans: For someone, the main thing is to take the right step in time.

examples.text: Ты не вовремя!

examples.text: Он всегда приходит вовремя.
